literature.paper: Leow, Nguyen & Chua (2021), Expert Systems with Applications 179, 115060
literature.comparison_level: DIRECT: paper's exact All-Weather ETF universe, exact train/test period, weekly rebalancing, same metrics (cumulative return, annual return, annual vol, max drawdown, Sharpe). Signal is substituted (our return-transformer mu vs their CNBC-tweet FinBERT sentiment), so this is a method-substitution head-to-head, not a signal replication.
notes: Universe = paper Section 3.1 / Table 2 asset-class All-Weather basket (VTI, TLT, IEF, GLD, DBC); this is the basket the paper reports its Table 6 metric table for.

Period = paper's exact split: train Aug-2018..Dec-2019, out-of-sample Jan-2020..early-Apr-2020, Yahoo Finance daily. NB: the paper's 'to April 2020' is EFFECTIVELY ~2020-04-03 -- that end date reproduces their Table 6 SPY (-23.2% vs -23.6%) and MPT (+3.4% vs +3.3%) cumulative returns; an Apr-30 cutoff overstates recovery (SPY only -10%). test_end pinned to 2020-04-03 for a same-window comparison.
Rebalancing = weekly (paper settled on weekly to reduce transaction costs).
MASTER is disabled: it is a cross-sectional model needing >=10 assets/day; the All-Weather basket has only 5. TFT and PatchTST run per-asset and are retained.
Cardinality K=5 = all assets eligible (non-binding), matching Leow's long-only no-cardinality All-Weather setup.

The paper's SPY buy-and-hold, CRB All-Weather and MPT (Max-Sharpe/Min-Vol) benchmarks are reproduced separately (benchmark reproduction script) and validated against Table 6; the engine only produces the transformer/Historical pipeline rows.

Five seeds (1, 7, 21, 42, 100); report mean +/- std across seeds, never a single-seed point value. NB: PatchTST spans -0.93..+3.09 across these seeds at P=0.5/PSO, so any single-seed number for this universe is meaningless.

CAVEAT: 4-month OOS (~17 weekly decisions) over a single COVID crash -> economic/directional read only, no statistical significance; tiny 5-asset / ~350-day-train cross-section stresses the transformers.

FAIRNESS/UNITS: horizon scaling (automatic) scales historical mu AND Sigma by the forecast horizon H so they live on the same H-period scale as the transformers' raw H-day mu. Without it the model mu was inflated ~H-fold against a 1-day Sigma, so the nominal P meant a different risk aversion per model (P'/(1-P')=c*P/(1-P)); PatchTST's weights were then identical at P=0.2/0.5/0.8, i.e. it was solving pure max-return while Historical solved real mean-variance. Scaling both moments is a no-op for the Historical solution (H factors out of the objective), so this repairs units only.

FAIRNESS/CADENCE: moment_refit=match_models re-estimates the historical mu/Sigma exactly when the models are retrained (model_refit), instead of the previous 'expanding' mode that refreshed the baseline every week while the transformers stayed frozen at fit_end. Both sides now act on the same information set.

FAIRNESS/RISK-MATCHING: the P grid is widened to 11 points so `python benchmark/run.py risk-matched --dir <output_dir>` can report every model at the P whose REALIZED annualized volatility matches the baseline's. Residual mu-dispersion differences (PatchTST still ~4x Historical after the unit fix) mean an equal-P read is still not an equal-risk read; the risk-matched table is the one to quote.

FAIRNESS/SEEDS: run_settings.seed_ensemble=true averages each model's mu across the 5 seeds before a single optimizer call (Gu-Kelly-Xiu style ensembling), applied uniformly to every model. This replaces reporting a mean +/- std over wildly dispersed single-seed Sharpes.
